# PremiseSQL: Evaluating Premise Critique and Abstention in Text-to-SQL Systems

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#premisesql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.22158v1) · arXiv:2610.22158v1, 15 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 46 PDF pages: main text and limitations, Appendices A-E, all construction/evaluation prompts, Tables 1-17 and Figures 1-29/case studies. Main behavior/mechanism plots visually checked; garbled figure-text extraction was resolved from page images.

## Research question

Detect flawed request premises and withhold misleading SQL without suppressing valid paired originals.

## Method

Creates 1,800 taxonomy-guided perturbation/original pairs and compares Base, Implicit and Explicit flaw prompts. Two judges score ordinal SQL behavior, flaw detection and subtype; separate analyses inspect failure operations.

## Evaluation

Sixteen models, paired query-level bootstrap comparisons and a 2,160-output human check. Execution validation covers 1,726 originals; GEN itself measures output presence. The 8,000-response mechanism sample excludes unrecoverable schema exposures.

## What the results support

Explicit flaw assertions increase detection but suppress SQL on valid controls. Overt contradictions are easier than ambiguity. Generation and conditional execution quality remain distinct despite their aggregate correlation.

## Limits and qualifications

Taxonomy-derived labels impose a critique policy, not formal SQL impossibility. Mechanism incidence is conditional on selected failures and is unweighted; its 300-example human validation preselects AI-consensus labels, so it is assisted rather than AI-blinded.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Paired originals expose over-refusal, but the static protocol does not measure resolving ambiguity through a live dialogue.

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
